section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that man's ability to act against the divine will stems from the unlimited capacity of Atzmus, and that through serving God with his own power, this capacity is revealed.
section.t: And corresponding to this is the matter in the service of man,
that this [ability] that man can do the opposite of the Supernal Will
[which is brought about by the tzimtzum,
as mentioned above]
is because Atzmus is not compelled by anything.
However, in this matter
[the power given to man to do the opposite of the Will],
the concept of the capacity of Atzmus is in the ultimate concealment and hiding.
And through man serving God, and the service is with his own power and his free choice,
[for although the Ein Sof is in every place and there is nothing apart from Him, nevertheless, since He, blessed be He, is all-capable, He created man in a way that he can serve with his own power],
through this it is revealed that the power of man's choice
(also that he can choose, heaven forbid, the opposite of the Will)
is from the capacity of Atzmus.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the previous idea to the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on the verse "And there was evening and there was morning," explaining that the wicked's deeds serve as a throne for the righteous, raising the question of whether God desires both.
section.t: And one can connect this with the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov
on the verse,
"And there was evening and there was morning, etc.,"
for it is brought in the Midrash,
"'And there was evening' — these are the deeds of the wicked, and 'and there was morning' — these are the deeds of the righteous,
and I do not know in which of them He delights,
[but] since it is written,
'And God saw the light, that it was good,'
it is [clear] that in the deeds of the righteous He delights."
And it is perplexing:
How could it enter the mind that He delights in the deeds of the wicked?
And the Baal Shem Tov explains,
that "there is benefit and advantage to the light from the darkness,"
meaning that the quality of the advantage of the light is recognized
from the aspect of the darkness,
and similarly the quality of the wise person is recognized
from the aspect of the fool,
the quality of the righteous from the aspect of the wicked, etc.
And this is [the meaning of] "and I do not know in which of them He delights,"
for since even the deeds of the wicked are a throne for the deeds of the righteous,
there is room to say that everything is included in one unity, heaven forbid,
therefore it is stated, "And God saw the light, that it was good" — these are the deeds of the righteous,
for regarding the deeds of the wicked, separation is needed.
[And based on this, he explains there the verse,
"I considered my ways, and turned my feet to Your testimonies,"
as will be explained below in section 13.]

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that the advantage of light from darkness refers to the possibility of free choice, and that the delight in the possibility of choosing evil is only because it reveals the capacity of Atzmus, but God specifically delights in the righteous.
section.t: And it needs to be understood:
That this [idea] that the advantage of light is recognized from the darkness is
(seemingly)
that through the deficiency of the darkness, the advantage of the light is recognized,
and how can it be said that because of this, even the deeds of the wicked
(darkness)
are included in one unity?
And it can be said,

that the intention in this, that the advantage of the light is recognized through the darkness, is that through the possibility to choose the deeds of the wicked, it is recognized that the deeds of the righteous are through their free choice,
service with their own power.
And since through service with one's own power it is revealed that even the possibility to choose the deeds of the wicked is from the capacity of Atzmus,
therefore there is room to say that He delights in the deeds of the wicked,
meaning that the delight above
[and also the revelation of His unity, blessed be He — is included in one unity]
is also in the possibility to choose the deeds of the wicked.
And therefore it is stated, "And God saw the light, that it was good,"
that He delights specifically in the deeds of the righteous.
